page: Amazon Web Services m8g.24xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by AWS Graviton processors. Built on the ARMv9 architecture, the server features 96 dedicated physical cores utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V2 model running at 2.8 GHz. It does not use simultaneous multithreading, providing exactly one thread per core across its 96 vCPUs. The hardware configuration includes 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance operates on the Nitro hypervisor, does not include local storage, and lacks a dedicated GPU. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 40 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates distinct performance characteristics, particularly in multi-threaded and memory-intensive operations. The server achieves top-tier status in multi-core CPU performance, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench multi-core metrics. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with cached small-block reads reaching 11,077.26 GB/sec and uncached large-block reads at 481.15 GB/sec. In contrast, single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average tier. This performance profile highlights a clear tradeoff: while individual core execution speeds are average, the massive parallel capacity of 96 dedicated cores delivers top-tier throughput for concurrent workloads.

The resource density of the ARM-based architecture provides high qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallelized enterprise applications. The server demonstrates top-tier efficiency in database operations, static web serving throughput at 111.67 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations processing 195.79 million operations per second. It also shows strong performance in software compilation and physics simulations. However, for large language model inference, a notable tradeoff exists: while text generation for 7B and 70B models ranks in the top tier, text generation for smaller 135M models is relatively weak. This server is best suited for multi-threaded workloads, containerized microservices, high-throughput web serving, and database management.
description: The Amazon Web Services m8g.24xlarge is an ARM64 general-purpose server instance powered by 96 dedicated AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 physical cores running at 2.8 GHz. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, it features 384.0 GB of system memory, 40 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and no local storage or GPU. Benchmarks reveal top-tier multi-core CPU performance, high memory bandwidth, and exceptional throughput in database operations, static web serving, and Redis SET operations. However, single-core performance remains average, presenting a tradeoff where parallel execution is highly prioritized over single-threaded speed. This hardware profile delivers qualitative cost efficiency for highly concurrent workloads, making it suitable for large-scale web serving, software compilation, database management, and multi-threaded enterprise applications.
